one_line_note: Opened Sep 13 2015 with the new 34 St-Hudson Yards station; first new subway station in over 25 years
Opened Jan 1 2017; Q line extended with new stations at 72 St 86 St and 96 St
Opened to the public Jan 1 2021 in the converted Farley Post Office building
Opened Jan 25 2023 with limited LIRR shuttle service; full service began Feb 27 2023
Four new East Bronx stations; MTA confirmed a three-year delay in Oct 2025 pushing the original 2027 target to roughly 2030
Q extension to 106 St 116 St and 125 St; 1.97 billion dollar tunneling contract awarded Aug 2025 with September 2032 revenue service target
Brooklyn-Queens light rail entered preliminary engineering Aug 2025 and environmental review Oct 2025; no construction start or opening date set

item: City of Yes for Housing Opportunity adopted
one_line_note: Council approved the modified zoning text Dec 5 2024 by a 31-20 vote; projected about 80000 homes over 15 years

item: Charter revision housing ballot proposals approved
one_line_note: Voters passed Props 2 3 and 4 on Nov 4 2025 fast-tracking affordable housing and streamlining land use review; Prop 5 (digital city map) also passed

item: Mamdani Block by Block housing plan released
one_line_note: Released May 26 2026; targets 200000 new affordable homes built and 200000 homes preserved over the next decade

item: SEQRA reform signed in FY27 state budget
one_line_note: Signed May 27 2026; exempts qualifying housing (up to 500 units in higher-density NYC zones) from environmental review and caps EIS completion at two years
